blocks.title: Split a message into packets
blocks.text: The sender can split data into separate packets or segments. Each includes control information such as addressing and/or sequence information at relevant protocol layers.

blocks.title: Packets may take different routes
blocks.text: Packet switching lets network traffic share links. IP forwarding can choose different paths; it does not guarantee the same arrival order.

blocks.title: Restore order when needed
blocks.text: TCP provides a reliable ordered byte stream, using acknowledgements and retransmission if required. Do not confuse TCP guarantees with best-effort IP delivery.

blocks.title: Worked example · Route
blocks.text: The network may forward them along different paths, so arrival order is not guaranteed.

blocks.title: Worked example · Receive
blocks.text: TCP uses sequence information to buffer out-of-order data.

blocks.title: Worked example · Deliver
blocks.text: When missing earlier bytes arrive, TCP makes data available to the application in the correct order: first 1, then 2.

blocks.title: Detect gap
blocks.text: The receiver recognises that data between segment 1 and segment 3 is missing.

blocks.title: Recover
blocks.text: TCP can cause the missing data to be retransmitted; once the gap is filled, data is delivered in order.
